## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2f923ae47993c2d89b5d32080676d35f1fb88aa4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bu-tree-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/queue-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/kernel-queue-membership.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts

Read: card #29738 (body, comments 6594482347, 6597517535, 6599161425), parent #29604 (body, comments 6588472222, 6589473271, 6591670782, 6594432222 — the ruling, letter B), PR #29865 body and file list, the net diff against `main` at the head (one file, +51/−1), the 46 check-runs on the head, and the cited code at `origin/main` `4b71a82b` (the branch base `42ff86f6` is 2 merges behind it; `approval-service.ts`, the authz middleware, `team-graph.ts` and `business-unit-graph.ts` moved there, none of it at the sites this ADR cites — the amendment is judged against the live tree).

### ① Derived judgments

- Face `rules`: `docs/adr/**` is a governed path, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and Tier H (the maintainer's approval) — right; the record's tier line and the card's claim name it.
- Accept sets: none move. The diff is ADR text — no schema, no code, no test, no changeset, no generated output. The status line keeps `Proposed` as its first keyword, so `scripts/adr-index.mjs` renders the same row (the new note sits past the index's truncation point) — right; `pnpm check:adr-index` and `check:adr-symbol-anchors` were green in the dev's local run and the CI docs-guard lane is success.
- No `!` and no narrowing arm on THIS PR — right: the ADR narrows no published behaviour; the D6/D7 doors narrow when the code half lands, and the ruling record says that half carries `!` and the dogfood battery.
- The two new symbol anchors (`approval-service.ts#warnExpansionFailed`, `ownership-queue-service.ts#queuesNaming`) resolve to live symbols at `origin/main` — right.
- Check-runs on the head: 46, all completed — 26 success, 20 skipped by path filter, 0 failure. Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, every Lint and Type Check lane, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core (1/8), Test UI and the Dogfood Regression Gate are success. The gate verdicts are green.
- One derived claim the text makes on a public contract: D2 says "the consumer says which it is owed when it calls". The spec contract already carries `QueueExpansionPurpose = 'access' | 'addressing'`, an axis about switched-off positions (D6 passes `addressing`; D7 passes nothing). Refuse-vs-nobody is a second, independent axis (D7 wants access-purpose AND refuse). The ADR leaves the spelling to the code half — right to leave, named here so the code half does not overload `purpose`.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` label, Check Changeset success, `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing — right.
- `Clause-②: no (ADR text only; no published accept set moves)` — the fleet reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) parses it as a declared `no` with no narrowing arm. Right for this PR; the narrowing declaration (`no (narrowing)`) belongs to #29604's code half, where the ruling puts it.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — right, no stored shape moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's open question (A: hold the `queue:` literal and warn the read failed; B: no slot, `onEmptyApprovers` decides)** — answered against the code: the MECHANISM of A is right and the CONSEQUENCE the note draws from it is wrong. A's mechanism is exactly the class PR #29602 landed for `team` and `position` (the expansion throws, `resolveApproverSpec`'s directory catch records `directoryFailure`, `warnExpansionFailed` says the read failed, the `type:value` literal is returned as the slot), and ruling B says the D6 slate "follows #29503's approvals failure class", so A is the reading the ruling asks for. But `openNodeRequest` decides the empty-slate policy with `slateNamesAPerson` (`approver-address.ts`: true only when some address on the slate carries no `:`), so a slate holding only `queue:NAME` is "no concrete approver" and takes the node's `onEmptyApprovers` route exactly as a `team:`-only slate does today: `admin_rescue` (the default) opens the request on the organization's administrators, `auto_approve` approves it, `fail` throws, `fallback` opens on the fallback slate. The note's "so the request waits rather than advances past the queue's people" and "`onEmptyApprovers` decides an empty slate as before and is not reached through a held slot" therefore do not hold, and the dev's reason for A over B ("under `auto_approve` B approves a request on an outage") applies to A equally whenever the queue is the node's only entry. Beside concrete people the held literal's effect depends on the node's behaviour (unanimous waits on the override; any/quorum advance on the others). Verdict on the flag: keep A's mechanism, rewrite its consequence — must-fix 1 under ④. Whether a failed queue read should NOT reach `onEmptyApprovers` at all (the node refusing to open, a class #29503 does not have) is a maintainer question for the Tier H approval, not a reading this review can make; escalated to the seat with that framing.
- Out-of-scope 1 (the `ownership-queue-service.ts` header's "Absence is not a fault" paragraph goes stale on merge, carrier #29604): accepted — the code half rewrites that file.
- Out-of-scope 2 (`QUEUE_READ_LIMIT` silent drop, comment 6591670782): accepted — the ruling record leaves it to the code half or a split with a recorded reason.
- Deviations (no PR subscription, no GitHub MCP, model-free trailers, PR-body shape, the two container restarts): process, none touches the ADR; accepted.
- `premise_still_valid: true`: checked — ruling B (6594432222) stands, no later ruling on #29604 or #29738.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0142-…md`, judged against its first consumer (the #29604 code half) and the execution plan, in the cited code at `origin/main`.

**What holds.**

- D2's empty/failed split matches the expander: `expandSpec` catches and answers `[]` once-warned, `holderCheck` catches and answers `false`, `authoredMemberSpecs` catches and counts authored members as nobody; the "absent table is absence" clause matches the sibling reads (`isObjectAbsentError` in `readRowsToCompletion`).
- Admission consumers keep nobody and nobody denies — verified at every site the D2 bullet names: D3 `sharing-service.ts#callerQueues` (catch to `[]`), `kernel-queue-membership.ts#resolveOnto` (catch, fails closed), `sitsInCallersQueue` through `isMember`; D4 the authz middleware's insert arm (`isMember` false → `denyQueueWrite`), the explain engine's `queueMember`; D5 `assignment-rules.ts` parks on both the `[]` branch and the thrown branch. Right.
- D7's isolation claim is true of the tree at every named pass: `evaluateRule` → `evaluateResolvedRule` → `desiredGrantsForRule` expands BEFORE `reconcile`, so a throw revokes nothing; `evaluateAllForRecord` has the #29362 per-rule catch; `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` expands before its chunked delete and both callers catch per rule (`queue-hooks.ts#recomputeQueueRecipientRules`, `bu-tree-recompute.ts` onGraphWrite, each warning with the rule); `reconcileRuleForUser` asks `ruleReachesUser` → `isMember` before its revoke loop and `recipient-membership-recompute.ts` catches per rule-and-user pair; `evaluateAllRulesForObject` catches per rule. `queuesNaming`'s catch answers `[]`, which only leaves the queue rules out of `affected` — it revokes nothing, as the note says. The BU module's "unreadable queue counts as affected" fallback then hands the rule to a pass that refuses. The code half owes only the refusing `expandMembers`/`isMember`. Right.
- D6's mechanism is reachable: the queue branch sits inside the resolver's try, the catch sets `directoryFailure`, and `queue:` is admitted by no acting path (`approver-address.ts`, position is the one literal prefix). One thing the code half must do that the note does not spell: today the `type === 'queue'` early return (the "expanded to nobody" warning, no slot) runs BEFORE the `directoryFailure` check, so a thrown expansion would still be reported as nobody; the queue branch has to consult `directoryFailure` first. The ADR prescribes the target, so this is the execution plan's, not a finding.

**Must-fix 1 — D6 note: two sentences are false against `openNodeRequest`.** "the slot is held as the `queue:` literal … so the request waits rather than advances past the queue's people" and "`onEmptyApprovers` decides an empty slate as before and is not reached through a held slot". `slateNamesAPerson` treats every `type:value` literal as no person, so a request whose slate holds only the held `queue:NAME` slot goes to `onEmptyApprovers`: on the default `admin_rescue` it opens on the administrators (past the queue's people), on `auto_approve` it is approved on an outage. That is the #29503 class as it stands for `team` today, and it is what the ruling asked the note to follow — so the fix is textual: say the literal is held and the failure is warned (never "expanded to nobody"), that beside concrete people the request's fate is the node's behaviour (unanimous waits on the override), and that a slate with no concrete person still takes the node's `onEmptyApprovers` route, as a `team` whose read failed does. Tier H text that promises a wait the code does not deliver is the one thing this record must not carry to the maintainer.

**Must-fix 2 — D2 note: the fault list omits the `sys_queue` row read, so the ruled defect stays reachable one table over.** `resolveQueue` reads `sys_queue` through `authoredQueueRow` (catch → `null`) and `authoredQueueNames` (catch → `[]`); for an authored queue a failed `sys_queue` read makes `expandMembers` answer `[]` and `isMember` `false` under the amendment's own "a name that resolves nowhere" — the EMPTY case. The recompute consumers then do exactly what the ruling refuses: D7 revokes every grant the queue gave, D6 warns "no queue of that name exists there". The amendment's principle ("Nothing is granted and nothing is revoked on an answer the expander could not stand behind") and its enumeration disagree, and the code half is bound to the enumeration. The list already holds `sys_queue_member`, which no specification reads either, so the intent is plainly "every read the expansion makes"; write that, name `sys_queue` in it, and say a queue that could not be resolved is not a queue that resolves nowhere.

**Should-fix 1 — D2:** "a thrown failure naming the specification and the table" — the `sys_queue_member` (and `sys_queue`) reads precede any specification; say "naming the read" so the code half is not asked to name a specification that does not exist.

**Should-fix 2 — D6:** item 2 spells the literal `queue:` + id; the note spells it `queue:` + name. The resolver writes `a.value`, a machine name under D1. Align item 2 (or say the two are one spelling) so the code half's pin has one literal to match.

- `Metadata-protocol: none` — right; no stored shape moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

Round-1 findings, each against the new head:

- **Must-fix 1 (replaced by ruling 6599731698)** — closed. The D6 note now states the ruled target rather than today's class: node refuses to open under every policy, loud, own error class, names the read, retryable, no parked state, team and position in the same class, replaces the "follows #29503's class" wording. The held-literal reading is withdrawn in the text and in the dev's addendum. Judged word by word under ④.
- **Must-fix 2 (`sys_queue` reads)** — closed. D2's fault sentence now opens "any read the expansion makes" and names `sys_queue` ("through which an authored queue resolves") and `sys_queue_member` ahead of the specification tables, with the sentence round 1 asked for: "A queue that could not be resolved is not a queue that resolves nowhere: the first is a failed read, the second is absence." Verified against `authoredQueueRow` (catch → `null`) and `authoredQueueNames` (catch → `[]`): a failed `sys_queue` read is now a fault under the text, not the empty case.
- **Should-fix 1 (naming a specification that may not exist)** — closed: "a thrown failure naming the read, never `[]`, `null` or `false`".
- **Should-fix 2 (literal spelling)** — closed: item 2 now reads `queue:NAME` "(the queue's machine name, D1, as the resolver writes an approver's `value`)" and the note uses the same spelling; D1's "referenced everywhere by its machine name … an approver's `value` (D6)" and the resolver's `${type}:${a.value}` agree.

The dev's addendum 6600440519: `open_questions` is empty — the round-1 question (hold the literal vs no slot) is mooted by the ruling. `out_of_scope_findings` (the queue service's "Absence is not a fault" header going stale on merge; `QUEUE_READ_LIMIT`'s silent drop; the purpose-axis warning) — all carried on #29604, accepted. `deviations` — the D6 note no longer cites #29503's class as the outcome (that is the ruling, not a deviation); two lines past 120 columns (no gate reads line length; `check:doc-authoring` and the docs-guard lane are green); one worker restart (process). None touches the ADR's meaning. `premise_still_valid: true` — checked: both rulings on #29604 stand and nothing later supersedes them. `body_amendments` — nine items the seat applies; the ADR text, not the body, is what this record judges.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0142-…md`, judged against ruling 6599731698 (B) and ruling 6594432222 (B), its first consumer (#29604's code half) and the cited code at `origin/main`.

**The D6 note states ruling B — phrase by phrase.** Trigger: "A failed read behind the queue (D2) refuses the slate, and the approval node then refuses to open" ↔ "when a directory read behind a queue, team or position approver fails, the approval node refuses to open". Policies: "under every `onEmptyApprovers` policy alike (`admin_rescue`, `auto_approve`, `fail`, `fallback`): not routed to the organization's administrators, not auto-approved and not opened on a fallback slate" ↔ the ruling's second sentence, and the enum has exactly those four. Failure shape: "an error class of its own — not `NO_APPROVERS`, not 'expanded to nobody' — that names the read that failed … retryable: the run is re-triggered once the directory reads again" ↔ the ruling's Retryable paragraph. Scope: "the ruling puts a `team` or `position` approver whose directory read failed in the same class, so the one node refusal covers the three" — queue, team and position, no narrower; and the D2 bullet plus the D7 note leave D3/D4/D5 and D7 where ruling 6594432222 put them, as the ruling requires. No extra scope: "No parked or auto-retry state is part of this decision; one that is wanted is its own card" is the ruling's own exclusion restated, not a state the ADR adds. Supersession: "it replaces the earlier wording of record 6594432222, under which a refused slate followed the approvals resolver's existing failure class" — right, and the history stays readable. The status line says the same in one clause.

**Every execution-point anchor exists and says what the ADR says.** `resolveApproverSpec`: `let directoryFailure: string | undefined` is declared before the `try` that wraps every directory expansion (team, BU, position, membership tier, queue, manager) and the cross-org read filter; the `catch` sets it ("already records the failure" — true, as a local of the resolver). The `type === 'queue'` branch below the try warns "expanded to nobody" and returns `[]` BEFORE the `if (directoryFailure !== undefined)` arm that the graph types reach — so "the `queue` branch's early 'expanded to nobody' return must consult it first" names a real ordering defect the code half must fix, exactly as the ruling spells it. `openNodeRequest`: the slate comes back from `expandApprovers` as a flat `string[]`, and the first decision on it is `if (!slateNamesAPerson(approvers))` → `emptyPolicy` — so "must see it and refuse before `slateNamesAPerson` hands the slate to `onEmptyApprovers`" names the exact seam; `slateNamesAPerson` answers true only when some address on the slate carries no colon, as round 1 read it. "Item 2's 'never written again' stays whole: a failed read writes no `queue:NAME` literal and no slot of any kind" holds under the target: a node that refuses to open persists no request row, so no slot of any spelling is stored; the empty case keeps item 2's "returns `[]`" and the node's `onEmptyApprovers`.

**D2's fault list against every read the expansion makes.** `expandMembers` → `resolveQueue` reads the activation ledger (`sys_metadata_activation`, for a declared name), `sys_queue` (`authoredQueueRow`) and `sys_queue_member` (`authoredMemberSpecs`); `expandSpecs` → `expandSpec` reads, per kind, `sys_team_member` (`TeamGraphService.expandUsers`), `sys_user_position` AND `sys_member` (`PositionGraphService.expandPositionUsers` unions the ADR-0057 D4 transition limb through `expandRoleUsers`; `holdsPosition` falls to `holdsRole` the same way), `sys_business_unit_member` and `sys_business_unit` (the BU tree); a `position` kind under the `access` purpose also reads the ledger (`positionActive`). The `sys_user` reads in the two graph services are `managerOf`, not on the queue path. Today every one of these failures is caught to nobody (`expandSpec` → `[]`, `holderCheck` → `false`, `authoredMemberSpecs` → no rows) except the ledger, which `switchedOff` catches to "treated as switched ON for this call". The text's binding clause — "any read the expansion makes" — covers all of it, and the ruled defect is no longer reachable by the enumeration alone, which is what round 1's must-fix asked for. The enumeration itself under-describes the tree in two places — should-fix 1 below.

**Admission consumers (D3/D4/D5)** — the bullet is unchanged from round 1 and the sites are unmoved: D5 `assignment-rules.ts` parks on both the `[]` branch ("no members … the row parks") and the thrown branch ("could not be read — the row parks"), which is what "a row parks in the queue (D5 says so already)" cites, and D5's own paragraph says a failed read leaves the row as it was and logs at `warn`. Right.

**D7 note** — the delta changes one phrase ("a failed read behind the queue (D2)"), and the passes it names still hold as round 1 verified: `evaluateRule` → `evaluateResolvedRule` → `desiredGrantsForRule` expands before `reconcile`; `evaluateAllForRecord` has the #29362 per-rule catch; `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` expands before its chunked delete; `reconcileRuleForUser` asks `ruleReachesUser` → `queues.isMember` (the holder check) before its revoke loop, and `recipient-membership-recompute.ts` catches per rule-and-user pair with "any write to the rule, or a restart" in its own warning. Right.

**Should-fix 1 — D2's enumeration names fewer reads than its quantifier.** (a) "the member tables a specification reads (`sys_user_position`, `sys_team_member`, `sys_business_unit_member`, the BU tree)" omits `sys_member`, which a `position` specification reads as the ADR-0057 D4 transition limb — the limb the filing addendum 6588472222 on #29604 put in this card; a failed `sys_member` read throws out of `expandPositionUsers` and is caught to nobody by `expandSpec` today, the ruled defect one table over. The binding clause covers it, so this is exactness, not a false promise: add `sys_member` to the parenthesis (or say "and the transition source a position reads"), so the code half's pin list is written from a complete sentence. (b) The activation ledger (`sys_metadata_activation`) is a read the expansion makes whose failure is NOT answered nobody — `switchedOff` leaves the declared default (on) for the call, the posture `positionConfersAccess` takes for the same ledger — and the sentence's reason ("the expander then knows nothing about who is in the queue") does not describe it. Under "any read … refuse", the code half would be asked to make the ledger refuse for D6/D7, diverging from every other reader of that ledger; say in one clause that the ledger read keeps its regime-C posture and is not a failed read in D2's sense, or that it is one. Either is acceptable; silence leaves the code half to choose.

**Should-fix 2 — the execution point names the primary slate only.** `openNodeRequest` resolves up to three slates through the same `expandApprovers`: the primary, a `fallback` policy's declared `fallbackApprovers`, and the administrators (as `user` entries). The note's "openNodeRequest must see it and refuse before `slateNamesAPerson` hands the slate to `onEmptyApprovers`" covers a failure on the primary slate; a `team` or `position` entry among `fallbackApprovers` whose read fails is reached inside the `fallback` arm, after that hand-off, and the ruling's "a directory read behind a … approver fails → the node refuses to open" applies to it equally. One clause — "on every slate the node resolves, the declared fallback slate included" — keeps "under every policy alike" honest for `fallback`'s own slate. Within the ruling, not extra scope; the code half can meet it either way, so should-fix.

For the code half, not findings: the resolver's `try` also wraps the cross-org read filter (`bounded`), so a failed read-filter lookup sets the same `directoryFailure` and will refuse the node under the same seam — consistent with the ruling, worth a pin; and `expandApprovers`'s `string[]` contract carries no failure today, so "openNodeRequest must see it" means the resolver throws (and the catch re-throws for the recompute case) or the contract grows a carrier — the ADR rightly leaves which to #29604.

Nothing the ADR now promises is false of the tree in a way the code half will not fix; each must-fix of round 1 is closed; the D6 note states ruling B with no wider and no narrower scope.
